title: Populate or perish
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 says reuse his-populate-or-perish, so to the Opus match check, as every reuse is
2026-11-20T12:25:51Z confirm: Claude Opus 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the same 1945 population-growth idea under Calwell at a depth that suits Stage 5, and its content and both questions are accurate and fair for NSW students.

confirm.reason: The bank point has the same title but is broader: it goes on to assisted passages and displaced persons, and one of its questions tests displaced persons. The new brief covers only Australia's small, mostly British population in 1945 and the aim to grow it for defence and industry, and it needs the 7 million figure the bank card lacks.

draft.title: Populate or perish
card: In 1945 Australia had about 7 million people. Most were of British background.
The government believed the country needed many more people. "Populate or perish" was a slogan of the time. It meant Australia must grow its population or risk being unable to protect itself.
World War II had shown how few people Australia had to defend a very large land, close to Asia.
More people would also mean more workers for factories and building projects, and more customers for what they made.
draft.remember: After WWII, Australia's government set out to grow the population to help defence and industry.

a.q: Why did the Australian government want a larger population after WWII?
opts: To help defend the country and build up industry
To reduce the number of people of British background
To cut the number of workers needed in factories
To make Australia's cities smaller and less crowded
a.why: The government linked a larger population to defence and to industry, which needed more workers. The wrong options would not have supported either aim, and a larger population does not make cities smaller.
a.clue: Think about the two reasons the card gives.

b.q: A newspaper in 1946 says: "Australia must populate or perish." What does the writer mean?
opts: The country needs more people to be safe and strong
The country has too many people for its food supply
The country should stop people from leaving it
The country must make its cities grow before its farms
b.why: The slogan warned that a small population left Australia open to risk, so growth was seen as necessary for safety and strength. It was not about too many people, because the problem seen at the time was too few.
b.clue: Was the worry too many people or too few?

a.best: To help defend the country and build up industry

b.best: The country needs more people to be safe and strong
